title: Linear Algebra Done Right
summary: This is a comprehensive mathematics textbook focused on abstract vector spaces and linear maps, intended for students who have had a previous introductory exposure to the subject. It emphasizes deep conceptual understanding through rigorous definitions, theorems, and proofs, notably avoiding the use of determinants until the final chapters.

title: Book of Proof
summary: This textbook provides a comprehensive introduction to mathematical proof techniques, covering fundamental topics such as set theory, logic, counting, and various methods of proof including induction and contradiction. It is designed for undergraduate mathematics students to transition from computational mathematics to rigorous proof-based reasoning.

title: Principles of Mathematical Analysis
summary: This is a classic undergraduate-level textbook on real analysis by Walter Rudin. It covers fundamental topics including the real and complex number systems, topology, sequences and series, differentiation, integration, and the Lebesgue theory.

title: Mathematics for Economists
summary: This document is the table of contents and introductory material for a comprehensive textbook on mathematical methods used in economic theory. It covers foundational topics including one-variable calculus, linear algebra, and the calculus of several variables, with specific applications to economic models.

title: Essential Mathematics for Economic Analysis
summary: This document is the front matter and table of contents for the fourth edition of a comprehensive mathematics textbook designed for economics students. It outlines the foundational algebraic, functional, and logical topics covered in the text, ranging from basic arithmetic to advanced mathematical modeling.

title: Real Analysis: Compactness, Continuity, and Differentiation
summary: These notes cover fundamental concepts in real analysis, including the properties of compact sets in Euclidean space, the Heine-Borel theorem, and the continuity of linear operators. The document also provides proofs for the Lipschitz continuity of linear maps and demonstrates that differentiability implies continuity.

title: Part IV: Probability Theory
summary: These notes provide a comprehensive overview of probability theory, covering fundamental concepts from probability spaces and random variables to expectation, conditional expectation, and stochastic convergence. The document bridges elementary computational methods with rigorous measure-theoretic foundations, specifically tailored for economics PhD students.

title: Introduction to Linear Algebra: Vector Spaces and Linear Maps
summary: These notes provide a foundational overview of linear algebra, covering vector spaces, subspaces, linear independence, and spanning sets. The document further explains the concepts of basis, change of basis, and the representation of linear maps as matrices.

title: Linear Algebra: Rank, Nullity, and Change of Basis
summary: These notes cover fundamental concepts in linear algebra, including the Rank-Nullity Theorem, invariant subspaces, and the mechanics of change of basis for linear transformations. It also introduces the definitions of matrix equivalence and similarity, as well as the concepts of direct sums and determinants.

title: Linear Algebra: Invariant Subspaces, Eigenvalues, and Inner Product Spaces
summary: These notes cover fundamental concepts in linear algebra, including invariant subspaces, eigenvalues, eigenvectors, and the process of diagonalization. The document also introduces inner product spaces, defining norms, orthogonality, and the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality.

title: Linear Algebra: Orthonormal Bases, Spectral Theorem, and Quadratic Forms
summary: These notes cover fundamental concepts in linear algebra, including the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality, the Gram-Schmidt process for orthonormalization, and the Spectral Theorem for real symmetric matrices. The document also explains the application of the Spectral Theorem to simplify quadratic forms and provides criteria for determining the definiteness of matrices using principal minors.

It includes formal definitions, proofs for key theorems like the Heine-Borel theorem, and examples of limit behavior for multivariable functions.

title: Linear Algebra: Guided Review and Exercises
summary: This document provides a guided review of linear algebra topics including linear systems, rank, null space, eigenvalues, and orthogonality. It includes both theoretical problems and worked solutions, culminating in an exploration of non-diagonalizable operators.

title: Linear Algebra: Guided Review and Exercises
summary: This document provides a structured review of linear algebra topics including linear systems, rank, null space, linear maps, eigenvalues, and orthogonality. It combines mini-lectures with worked examples and practice problems, including proofs and computational exercises.

title: Multivariate Calculus and Linear Algebra Problem Set
summary: This document contains a comprehensive set of practice problems covering multivariate calculus (homogeneity, convexity, implicit function theorem, integration) and linear algebra (subspaces, norms, linear independence, matrix rank, and diagonalization). It includes both theoretical proofs and computational exercises, with some sections providing worked solutions for specific problems.

title: Math Camp Recitation 1: Linear Algebra Exercises and Solutions
summary: This document contains a set of linear algebra exercises covering rank, subspaces, diagonalization, and matrix definiteness. Each exercise is followed by a detailed, step-by-step solution explaining the underlying mathematical concepts and proofs.

title: Math Camp Recitation 1: Linear Algebra Exercises
summary: This document contains a set of linear algebra exercises covering rank, systems of equations, subspaces, diagonalization, and matrix definiteness. Each exercise is followed by detailed worked solutions.

title: Math Camp Recitation 2: Linear Algebra Exercises
summary: This document provides detailed solutions to linear algebra exercises covering change of basis, inner product spaces, and idempotent matrices. It explains the relationship between coordinate transformations, Gram-Schmidt orthogonalization, and matrix decompositions like Cholesky.

title: Linear Algebra Recitation Exercises: Basis, Change of Basis, and Inner Product Spaces
summary: This document contains a set of linear algebra exercises covering column spaces, kernels, change of basis, transition matrices, and inner product spaces. It includes problem statements followed by detailed worked solutions for each exercise.

title: PhD Math Camp 2026 Syllabus
summary: This document is the official syllabus for the 2026 PhD Math Camp at Columbia University. It outlines the course objectives, schedule, recommended references, and the mathematical topics covered, including linear algebra, real analysis, multivariable calculus, optimization, and probability.

title: Probability Lecture Notes: Foundations and Expectations
summary: These lecture notes cover fundamental concepts in probability theory, including Kolmogorov axioms, conditional probability, Bayes' Rule, and the properties of random variables. The document also details joint distributions, marginal densities, expectation, variance, and the law of iterated expectations.

title: Analysis: Guided Exercises
summary: This document contains a series of guided exercises covering fundamental topics in real analysis, including topology, continuity, compactness, multivariate differential calculus, and the inverse/implicit function theorems. It emphasizes proof techniques and conceptual understanding through guided steps and counterexamples.

title: PhD Mathematics Camp Comprehensive Practice Sheet
summary: This document contains a comprehensive set of 42 practice problems covering linear algebra, topology, differential calculus, optimization, and probability theory. It is designed for independent study for students preparing for advanced mathematics in economics.

title: Real Analysis: Guided Exercises
summary: This document provides a series of guided exercises covering fundamental topics in real analysis, including topology in R^n, continuity, compactness, differentiability, and the inverse/implicit function theorems. It includes detailed proofs and explanations for each problem, focusing on rigorous analytical techniques.

title: 2021 Mathematical Economics Exam
summary: This document is a 2021 exam covering mathematical methods in economics, including real analysis, linear algebra, optimization theory, and correspondences. It contains a mix of theoretical true/false questions with proofs and applied optimization problems involving utility maximization and log-linearization.

title: Advanced Analysis and Optimization Exam
summary: This document contains a comprehensive set of advanced mathematics problems covering metric spaces, linear algebra, multivariable calculus (Jacobians and Taylor approximations), and constrained optimization. It includes detailed worked solutions for the initial problems regarding metric space properties and the discrete metric.

title: Analysis in Euclidean Spaces
summary: This document provides a comprehensive introduction to analysis in Euclidean spaces, covering real number completeness, topology, continuity, differentiation, and integration. It is designed for PhD-level mathematics preparation, focusing on the analytical foundations required for economic modeling.

title: Linear Algebra Lecture Notes
summary: These lecture notes provide a comprehensive introduction to linear algebra, covering vector spaces, linear maps, determinants, eigenvalues, and inner product spaces. The text emphasizes the structural relationship between abstract linear maps and their matrix representations, with applications relevant to economics.

title: Optimization, Convexity and Correspondences
summary: This document provides a comprehensive overview of optimization theory, covering convex geometry, concave functions, and optimization in Euclidean space. It further explores equality and inequality-constrained optimization, duality, parameterized optimization, and fixed-point theorems, with specific applications to economic models.
